chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'd, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant: Is it permissible to sell and buy them for the one who makes combs from them? He said, 'There is no harm; indeed, my father had a comb or combs from it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell and buy elephant bones for making combs in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the commercial trade of elephant bones for crafting combs, grounding the ruling in the precedent of the Imams' own usage. This establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of permissibility) through the practical habits of the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing that items not explicitly prohibited are generally lawful for trade and use.
